turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: What brings you in?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So I've had a fever that I measured this morning and I had a cough.  I've had a cough these last several days. Yeah, today is Friday so it started Monday, so I guess like yeah the cough started four days ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and the fever started four days ago as well?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Well, I've been feeling hot this week, but I checked my temperature this morning and it was the first time I checked it and it was 38.5.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so that's definitely a fever, so we can take your temperature today as well. Umm, so have your symptoms been the same or getting worse, or be getting better over the past few days?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: They are getting worse. I've been starting to feel really fatigued and, uh, tired as well and the cough has gotten worse too.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you ever felt like this before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I mean, maybe a really long time ago when I was a kid or something like that. Maybe I had the flu, but nothing recently.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And do you have a sore throat at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No sore throat. It does get a little scratchy with my cough but hasn't been sore.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and do you have any issues swallowing food?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, but I haven't been as hungry.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, you haven't been as hungry. Um, have you had any changes to your taste?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I feel like I've been tasting my food OK.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about smell?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I feel like I've been able to smell.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, do you have a runny nose or a blocked nose? Do you feel congested?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Maybe a little runny, but not too bad.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about your hearing or vision? Any changes there?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I haven't noticed anything.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any pain or discharge from either your ears or eyes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so let's go back to the cough. Um, are you producing any sputum?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No sputum.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so it's a dry cough?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah it is.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any blood associated with the cough?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I haven't seen any blood.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, do you feel wheezy at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I haven't noticed any wheezing.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about shortness of breath?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Usually well, after some of my coughing fits, I can be a little bit shorter in breath, but otherwise they've been.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any chest pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I haven't had any chest pain.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Do you ever feel like your heart's racing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and any night sweats or chills?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I have felt a little chilly at night, but I haven't had any night sweats.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how about weight loss? Have you had any weight loss over the past few months?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, it's been about the same. Maybe down a few pounds over this week as I just haven't been eating as much.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, yeah. Umm, does anything make the cough better or worse?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Umm, no, I can't think of anything.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how have your bowel movements been?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: They've, I would say they've been normal.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and any abdominal pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No pain, but I have been a little nauseous.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Nauseous, OK. Have you thrown up?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I haven't vomited, but I've certainly felt like it a few times.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and any triggers for your nausea?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh I can't think of anything. It just sort of came on. And it really went away on its own pretty quickly, but uh I don't know, maybe it was when I had my headache.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, when when did your headache start?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, so it's been on and off these last several days so I've been kind of resting a bit more too.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK yeah, you said past several days, have you ever had headaches before that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I've had, I think they're called tension headaches. I get those every so often and will take Advil or something like that for them, and they usually go away.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Do these headaches feel like the same headaches?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, they they feel about the same, kind of like a pressure or vice grip on my head.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so it's not like the worst headache you've ever experienced?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I think it's just been a part of how I haven't been feeling well these these last few days.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, yeah. Do you feel fatigued or tired at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, for sure. I haven't really had any changes, but just haven't been really getting my work done throughout the day because I have just been feeling so tired.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, umm, and do you feel any sort of body aches that go along with your fatigue?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Maybe a little.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Umm, can you think of anything that may have caused your symptoms? You know, have you been in contact with anyone who's been sick recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I can't think of anybody I've been around who's been sick, but last weekend I went shopping in the mall so I went into quite a few stores.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and you were wearing your mask? Everyone else was wearing their mask?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, everybody far as I could tell.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you traveled anywhere recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, I've just been home.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, I just want to ask you a few more questions. Any memory loss or confusion?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any dizziness or fainting spells?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nothing like that, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Are you otherwise healthy?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, yeah I've well, I've been told I had high cholesterol so I've been taking Rosuvastatin for that the past few years.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and is it helping with the cholesterol levels?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, the last time I was at the family doctor I was told they were at a good level. O

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, good.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I'm sorry I'm pre-diabetic as well.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, when was the last time you had blood work done?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: : I think, uh six months ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and that's when you were told you were pre-diabetic?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I think my A1C was like 6.2% so uh, on the cusp.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, yeah, that's understandable. Um, have you made any sort of lifestyle changes to get your blood glucose under control?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Well, I have been walking the dog more. he weather is getting better and trying to eat out less often. Yeah, I've been trying to lose weight, but it it's been yeah, relatively stable still.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, we can review some options with you later on in the visit if you would like.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, certainly we can talk about that later.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, sounds good. Have you had any surgeries or hospitalizations in the past?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah I had an inguinal hernia repaired about five years ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And are you on any medications?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Just Rosuvastatin right now.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and any over the counter medications or herbal supplements?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Just a multi vitamin.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, umm, do you have any allergies?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Penicillin. I break out in hives.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and did you need to be treated with any sort of antibiotics recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no, I haven't had any antibiotics for a long time.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and are you up to date with all your immunizations?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I am, yeah, I get the flu shot every year.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, good. An yeah, that's really good. Um, do you know if you have any family history of any lung conditions or heart conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about cancers in the family?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I think my grandfather had bladder cancer, but, uh, I'm not sure.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and I forget if I asked you earlier, but have you had any changes to your urinary habits, any changes in your urine itself or voiding frequency?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I haven't had any changes there and I haven't noticed any like blood or color changes. No pain.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, great. And do you smoke?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, no I do not.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about marijuana?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nope.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any other recreational drug?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I just have a few beers on the weekend. Like probably I don't know two or three on Saturday and Sunday.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and where do you live?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I live in a like duplex and rent the basement in a house nearby.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, do you live with anyone?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I live with my girlfriend.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and um, any concerns for you know old carpets or mold or asbestos in the duplex that you're living in?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Not in our unit so I mean, maybe upstairs, but if it's anything like our place, then no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. I think those were all the questions that I had for you. Did you have any questions or concerns that you wanted to bring up before we end the interview?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, well  I guess I was just concerned about about COVID.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, you know that's the top on my list of differential diagnosis for you. So what we'll do is a COVID swab and that should come back in a day or so, but we do encourage isolation for 14 days and that includes from your girlfriend as well. So even if the COVID swab comes back negative, sometimes it can be false negative, so as long as you're having these symptoms, and these symptoms are common in COVID,  we do ask that you isolate for 14 days if the swab comes back positive. We will also notify public health so that they can get in touch with you and do some contact tracing to see where you may have gotten COVID from, but other than that, if it's not COVID, it could likely be another upper respiratory viral illness because of this time of year. A lot of different viruses are going around like common viruses or the flu, you know, so it could be one of those. And then if you're still sick or your symptoms change, we can reassess to make sure it's not a bacterial infection or bacterial pneumonia, in which case we can prescribe antibiotics.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK yeah, thank you for all that information. Sounds great.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, well take care then, alright.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Thank you.
